reviews.rationale: This abstract describes HRAS-driven brain vascular malformation with generic 'altered TGF-β signaling' and tip/stalk gene abnormalities, but contains no gene-specific data on Tnfrsf11b or Slc1a1. Neither supplied gene of mechanism 3 is studied here.

evidence_span.text: Overexpressing wild-type-Kir2.1 in endothelium of arteries from obese mice resulted in full recovery of the flow response.

reviews.rationale: Dominant-negative knockdown and overexpression experiments causally establish Kir2.1 (Kcnj2) as the flow-sensitive channel mediating endothelial mechanotransduction, matching the mechanism's claim. Tissue is mesenteric artery endothelium rather than brain, consistent with the declared partial (same cell type, different vascular bed) context.

evidence_span.text: NRP1 enables CDC42 activation and CDC42-dependent actin dynamics and filopodia extension in ECM-stimulated ECs, independently of VEGF-A signaling.

reviews.rationale: This paper directly and causally establishes the regulator claim that NRP1 activates CDC42 to drive endothelial tip-cell filopodia formation, using mouse hindbrain, zebrafish, and human EC models. Angpt2 appears only as an incidental qPCR marker gene, not as a substantively investigated supplied gene, so no supplied-gene credit applies; embryonic hindbrain vs. postnatal brain vasculature supports a partial context call.

evidence_span.text: The down-regulation of Kir2.1 reduced OSS-induced EPC mesenchymal transdifferentiation.

reviews.rationale: Knockdown and overexpression of Kir2.1 (Kcnj2) in endothelial progenitor cells causally link the channel to oscillating-shear-induced mesenchymal transdifferentiation, matching the specific mechanism clause about Kcnj2 in EPCs. The system (cultured EPCs, carotid injury model) is a different cell/tissue context from brain endothelium, consistent with the declared indirect label.

evidence_span.text: we uncover a reinforcing role for angiopoietin 2 at the BBB.

reviews.rationale: Using reverse genetics in pericyte-deficient brain, the paper finds ANGPT2 plays a BBB-reinforcing (stabilizing) role, explicitly noted as paradoxical relative to its canonical TEK-antagonist, vessel-destabilizing function claimed in the mechanism summary. Context (brain, BBB, single-cell) is directly on-target even though the functional direction opposes the cited destabilizing/pro-sprouting claim.
